title: Supreme Court's Lazaro-Javier retires with no overdue cases
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has appointed former COA chair Gamaliel Cordoba to succeed her.

blocks.text: Supreme Court Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier speaks at an event as seen in a video posted August 2024.

MANILA, Philippines — Supreme Court Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier retired Monday, November 16, with the high court recognizing her for maintaining a zero-backlog docket throughout her judicial career.
Lazaro-Javier was conferred the Judicial Medal of Distinction, one of the Supreme Court's highest honors for judicial excellence, during a retirement ceremony held on October 27.
The award is given to retiring justices who leave no cases undecided beyond the 24-month period prescribed by the Constitution.

"Given to retiring members of the SC who leave no cases undecided beyond the Constitution's prescribed 24-month period, the medal recognizes distinguished judicial service that helps sustain the people's faith and confidence in the Judiciary," the Supreme Court said in a statement Monday.
The high court said Lazaro-Javier maintained a zero-backlog docket both at the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. appointed former Commission on Audit chair Gamaliel Cordoba on November 13 to succeed Lazaro-Javier.
Cordoba is Marcos' third appointee to the Supreme Court, including the appointment of a new chief justice.
